applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Egypt has a broad network of bilateral investment treaties; applicability and current force must be verified for each investor's country of nationality and any treaty succession or termination measures.
Egypt–United States Income Tax Treaty, in force; it is a tax treaty, not an investment treaty.
Egypt is a party to the African Continental Free Trade Area Agreement and the Common Market for Eastern and Southern Africa Treaty; benefits depend on applicable rules and the transaction.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Principal AML statute: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended, and its Executive Regulations issued by Prime Ministerial Decree No. 951 of 2003, as amended. Company formation and company-record obligations are principally governed by Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 and its Executive Regulations, as amended, and the Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 where applicable. Companies must identify and retain beneficial-ownership information under applicable company and AML requirements and provide it to competent authorities. Confirm the current filing mechanism, prescribed form, and any subsequent amendments with GAFI and the competent Commercial Registry before filing.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation or commercial-register extract for each foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or equivalent competent authority in the shareholder's country of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing country and document qualify under the Apostille Convention; otherwise consular legalization through the Egyptian diplomatic or consular mission and Egyptian Ministry of Foreign Affairs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution or equivalent authorization approving the Egyptian LLC investment and appointing its representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board or other competent governing body of the foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization where required by the document's place of execution, followed by Hague Apostille where available or consular legalization; Arabic translation by an accepted translator may be required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of attorney for incorporation and related filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each foreign individual or corporate shareholder granting authority
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization, followed by Hague Apostille where available or consular legalization; Arabic translation and local formalities as required by the receiving authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or national identity document of each individual shareholder, manager, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport or identity-document authority in the person's country of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified copy and authentication as requested by GAFI, the Commercial Registry, or the receiving bank; apostille or consular legalization is not automatically required for every copy

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign shareholder good-standing certificate, where requested
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar or equivalent competent authority in the shareholder's country of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available or consular legalization; Arabic translation as required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding and periodically thereafter, identify and risk-assess domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates; screen shareholders, controllers, directors, authorized signatories, and UBOs against applicable United Nations Security Council sanctions, Egyptian domestic restrictions, and relevant transaction-specific sanctions regimes. OFAC screening is not a universal Egyptian statutory requirement but is commonly required by US-linked banks, payment providers, and counterparties. Apply risk-based enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth checks where warranted, and document screening results and escalation decisions. Confirm current lists and provider requirements at the time of each screening.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) electronic services and Egypt Business platform; company-name and commercial-register procedures may involve GAFI and the competent Commercial Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must comply with Egyptian Companies Law and the applicable registry's requirements, be distinguishable from existing registered names, and not be misleading or contrary to public order. Arabic is the principal language of Egyptian official filings; an Arabic name is generally required or recorded, and any foreign-language rendering must be consistent with the approved name and registry practice. Verify proposed Arabic spelling and transliteration directly with GAFI before execution of formation documents.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names implying government, ministry, public authority, or official sponsorship without authorization
Names suggesting a bank, financial institution, insurer, or regulated financial activity without the required approval
Names using protected state, national, religious, or international organization designations without consent
Words or descriptions that are misleading, contrary to public order or morals, or likely to confuse with an existing registered company or trademark
Regulated professional or licensed-activity terms where the company lacks the required authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain written confirmation of the reservation period and any renewal option from GAFI or the competent Commercial Registry at the time of application; the applicable period can depend on the certificate and procedure. If rejected, request the reason in writing, revise the name to address similarity or restricted wording, and resubmit through the same service. For a reviewable administrative decision, submit a reasoned written grievance to the issuing authority within the applicable statutory or stated deadline, attach evidence of distinctiveness and any required consent, and pursue the legally available administrative or judicial review route. Do not assume an extension or appeal suspends expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An Egyptian registered address is required. A serviced or virtual office may be acceptable for registration if it provides a genuine, verifiable address and the required lease, occupancy, or address evidence is accepted by GAFI, the Commercial Registry, and the tax authority. Acceptance is not assured for an e-commerce retailer; banks and payment providers may require evidence of actual management, inventory, fulfillment, and operating activity. A warehouse, customs, consumer-protection, or other sector approval may be required if the operating model involves those activities, notwithstanding that online retailing itself is specified as unlicensed.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Not reliably quantifiable from statute. Treat the risk as non-zero: tax, commercial, licensing, and other competent authorities may verify the registered address, and banks or payment providers may conduct independent site or documentary checks. Maintain accessible premises or a defensible serviced-office arrangement and retain lease, utility, and operating records.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Egyptian Companies Law No. 159 of 1981 as amended by Law No. 4 of 2009 and Law No. 17 of 2019, Articles 1-16 (Limited Liability Companies); read together with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Articles 2 and 4, and its Executive Regulations (Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2310 of 2018) establishing the GAFI One-Stop Shop.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration and One-Stop Shop Directorate, in coordination with the Commercial Registry Directorate, Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Incorporation Contract (Meethaq Al-Taassiss / Aqd Al-Tasees) executed before a licensed Notary Public or through GAFI electronic notarization services, filed via the GAFI One-Stop Shop portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for LLCs under Law 159 of 1981 as amended; however, the capital stated in the incorporation contract must be fully subscribed and deposited into a dedicated Egyptian bank account in the company's name, evidenced by a bank capital deposit certificate issued not more than five days prior to filing with GAFI.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTIONS OF THE FOUNDERS AND FIRST BOARD OF MANAGERS OF [COMPANY NAME] - EGYPT LLC. 1. RESOLVED, that the capital subscription schedule annexed to the incorporation contract is ratified in full, each founding shareholder's contribution having been paid to the company's dedicated Egyptian bank account. 2. RESOLVED, that the registered office is adopted at the address designated in the incorporation contract, Cairo, Egypt, and management is instructed to file the lease certificate and utility documents with GAFI. 3. RESOLVED, that [Name] is appointed General Manager and [Name] is appointed Compliance Officer, each with signatory authority, to hold office for the company's statutory term. 4. RESOLVED, that the General Manager is authorized to complete commercial registration, tax registration, and all ancillary statutory filings.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Trade name reservation and activity classification screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop (electronic portal or in-person at GAFI headquarters, Cairo)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File three proposed trade names in Arabic and English through the GAFI name reservation module; obtain the preliminary name approval certificate; verify that ISIC 4791 (internet retailing of outdoor camping equipment) is pre-cleared for LLC commercial registration without a special license; pay the nominal reservation fee and print the official name clearance certificate.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of all individual founders
Certificate of incorporation of each corporate founder, if applicable
Power of attorney of the authorized signatory founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a proposed name conflicts with an existing registered mark or trade name, file the alternate names immediately in the same GAFI session; a formal administrative objection against an erroneous rejection may be submitted to the GAFI Legal Department within 15 days of the rejection notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and notarization of the incorporation contract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice Notary Public or GAFI electronic notarization desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the incorporation contract in Arabic including founders' details, capital allocation, share subscription percentages, management structure, term of 25 years renewable, and the registered office's address; ensure all pages are initialed by every founder; execute the contract before the notary or via GAFI's e-notarization service and obtain the attested notarized copy for filing.
required_dossiers: Draft incorporation contract in Arabic (counter-signed by all founders)
Criminal record certificate (Fair Sheet) for each manager
Certified passport copies and proof of residence of each founder
Articles of association pro forma duly completed
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the notary issues a deficiency note, correct the stipulated clauses and re-attest within a 7-day GAFI cure period; a fully rejected attestation may be re-submitted once the underlying legal objections raised by the GAFI legal reviewer are remedied.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank account opening and deposit of paid-up capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian commercial bank licensed by the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary in-capital / escrow account in the pending company's name at a CBE-licensed bank; deposit the subscribed paid-up capital in Egyptian pounds or an acceptable foreign currency; obtain the bank certificate of capital deposit addressed to GAFI and dated within five business days of the incorporation filing.
required_dossiers: Passport copies and KYC forms for all signatories
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank places a KYC hold or requests supplemental documentation, provide the enhanced due diligence pack (bank statements, source of wealth evidence) within the bank's internal review window; any CBE compliance query is cured by a sworn source-of-funds declaration approved by the bank's AML compliance officer.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI incorporation application and issuance of the certificate of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI One-Stop Shop - Company Registration Department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the complete dossier through the GAFI One-Stop Shop either electronically or in person; pay the consolidated official filing fee (approximately USD 700 equivalent); respond to any same-day validation queries; upon approval, receive the electronic and physical Certificate of Incorporation bearing the company's registration number; GAFI then transmits the file ex officio to the Commercial Registry and the Egyptian Tax Authority.
required_dossiers: Notarized lease contract and utility bill as proof of registered office
Criminal record certificate of each manager and founder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If GAFI issues a query letter, cure the specified deficiencies within 15 days of notification; failure to cure triggers a deemed rejection, which may be appealed administratively per the GAFI internal grievance mechanism or by re-filing a corrected application without additional substance penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commercial Registry and tax authority registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Registry Office (within GAFI One-Stop Shop); Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: GAFI automatically forwards the incorporation file to the Commercial Registry for issuance of the commercial register extract (Al-Sijill Al-Tijari); simultaneously register with the ETA for the tax card (Bitaqa Darbiya) and obtain the VAT certificate under Law No. 67 of 2016, completing corporate income tax, payroll tax, and VAT registration in a single consolidated procedure.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of directors and beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Commercial Registry rejects the registration, correct the technical defect and re-file within 30 days without re-incurring the full incorporation fees; ETA tax card queries are cured by submitting the missing declaration forms and a cover letter addressed to the ETA Registration Directorate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social insurance, gazette publication, and municipal premises licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Organization for Social Insurance (NOSI); Official Gazette (Al-Waqa'i' Al-Misriyya); Local Municipal District Licensing Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the LLC as an employer with NOSI within 14 days of the first staff hire or immediately upon formation if hiring is imminent; pay the publication fee and submit the incorporation notice for the official gazette; file the commercial registry extract with the local district office to obtain the commercial premises license for the registered office and warehouse, if any.
required_dossiers: Gazette publication request and fee receipt
Municipal premises license application with lease and civil defense approval
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: NOSI penalty notices resulting from late filing are cured by submitting payroll records and a waiver request letter within the inspection deadline; gazette publication errors are corrected via a sworn correction statement; municipal license refusals are appealable to the Governorate's licensing committee within 30 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Licensing Directorate; Industrial Development Authority (IDA) is not engaged for purely internet retail activities under ISIC 4791, as no industrial manufacturing or processing operation exists in this business scope.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operation or manufacturing permit is mandated for ISIC 4791 internet retailing of outdoor camping gear; the LLC operates solely under the Commercial Registry Extract, the GAFI certificate of incorporation, and, where applicable, the local municipal commercial premises license covering the administrative office and warehousing area.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C - Environmental Self-Declaration / Exempt; the retail warehousing and office use of outdoor camping equipment does not trigger the mandatory Full Environmental Impact Assessment Report or the limited EIA scoping study under the EEAA EIA Listing Regulations; a simple environmental self-registration may be filed if gross storage area exceeds 500 square meters.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge or VOC emissions thresholds apply to this non-manufacturing activity; compliance is limited to municipal solid waste segregation and disposal under Law No. 202 of 2020 on waste management; any incidental packaging waste must be handled through contracted licensed waste collectors; general housekeeping and workplace exposure limits under Occupational Safety and Health Law No. 12 of 2003, Article 208 apply to the warehouse operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Civil Defense Fire Safety Certificate (Al-Himaya Al-Madaniya) required for any warehouse or office premises exceeding 100 square meters, conditioned on a successful structural load inspection and fire prevention inspection by the local Civil Defense Directorate; issuance of the commercial premises license is also conditioned on obtaining workplace occupational health and safety clearance from the competent governorate inspection office under Labor Law No. 12 of 2003.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Official portal: www.eta.gov.eg
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign and non-resident entities must register for a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and obtain a Tax Card through the ETA online portal by submitting certified constitutional documents, a local tax representative mandate (if applicable), proof of Egyptian business activity, and relevant licenses. E-commerce suppliers may use the simplified registration procedure introduced for non-resident direct sellers under Law No. 91 of 2005 and VAT Law No. 67 of 2016.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not provide pass-through check-the-box elections. An Egyptian LLC is discretionarily taxable at the corporate level. Available mechanisms include: VAT group registration election (per ETA Decision No. 114 of 2020), consolidated corporate tax filing election for resident corporations (subject to ETA approval and minimum ownership thresholds), and OECD-aligned hybrid mismatch limitation elections. No branch-level imputation election is permitted for LLCs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under Law No. 67 of 2016
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual taxable turnover (mandatory registration threshold); non-resident suppliers supplying digital or remote services to Egyptian consumers must register regardless of turnover if sales exceed EGP 500,000 annually
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: ETA e-invoicing is mandatory for VAT taxpayers in staged phases. All B2B and B2C transactions handled through approved channels must be transmitted in near-real-time to the ETA portal/API, validated, and returned with a UUID and QR code. E-receipt (POS) integration is mandatory for merchant transactions. Failure to obtain ETA clearance invalidates the invoice for VAT recovery.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods physically delivered outside Egypt are zero-rated. Services rendered to non-residents and used wholly outside Egypt are also zero-rated when supported by proper evidence. Zero-rating requires proof of physical export, receipt of foreign currency through Egyptian banking channels, and ETA pre-approval for recurring export exemption in limited cases.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate (Arabic: شهادة استلام الحصيلة)
Commercial sales invoice and the underlying export contract
Bank transfer receipt evidencing foreign currency proceeds received in Egypt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The ETA and Customs Authority may retroactively claw back zero-rated output VAT if export evidence is deficient or proceeds are not fully repatriated within the 180-day window. Penalties include late-payment interest of 2% per month, administrative fines up to EGP 50,000 per fiscal violation, and criminal fines of up to 100% of tax evaded for fraudulent zero-rating, customs declaration forgery, or deliberate under-invoicing. Executive officers may be subject to personal liability and imprisonment for serious evidential fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE) acting as the national foreign exchange administrator under Law No. 194 of 2020 and CBE Foreign Exchange Regulations issued pursuant to the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 88 of 2003, as amended.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-floating, partially convertible currency regime for the Egyptian Pound (EGP). Current account transactions, including trade-related payments and service fees, are generally permitted through licensed banks. Capital account transactions, including equity injections, shareholder loans, and dividend repatriation, require CBE registration/approval and supporting documentation. Profit remittance is permissible on presentation of audited financial statements, corporate tax clearance, and evidence that the capital was introduced through licensed banks and registered with CBE/Ministry of Investment. Practical constraints include periodic USD liquidity tightness, EGP devaluation risk, and enhanced bank-level documentation checks, which can delay remittances.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be received into an account of the Egyptian exporter at a licensed Egyptian bank and fully repatriated to Egypt within 90 days from the date of shipment. There is no mandatory statutory conversion of retained export proceeds into EGP, but the exporter must evidence the corresponding customs export declarations and CBE settlement forms. Any delay in repatriation without a CBE-approved waiver subjects the exporter to penalties, suspension of export facilities, and enhanced AML/KYC review.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operational Account / Multi-currency Account (EGP, USD, EUR)

Corporate Treasury Account / Operational Account with FX Hedging Line
Corporate Operational Account / Capital Escrow Account
Corporate Multi-currency Account / Cross-border Liquidity Concentrator

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low — Offshore digital EMI and payment/e-money institutions are not CBE-licensed and cannot lawfully provide local EGP clearing, hold Egyptian corporate accounts, or access CBE settlement systems. They may be used only as ancillary multi-currency wallets outside Egypt for collections in third countries; they are not viable as the primary treasury or clearing rail for an Egyptian LLC. Their use increases wire-trail opacity and may trigger enhanced KYC/AML scrutiny at local banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical or notarized appearance of authorized directors/signatories is generally required for corporate account opening. Some CBE-licensed banks permit remote/video onboarding only under approved e-KYC frameworks and only for low-risk, non-PEP entities with a verifiable local corporate registry record. In practice, leading Egyptian banks require at least one director to attend in person or to grant a notarized power of attorney to a local representative before final bank sign-off.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated LLC with no operating history and no established business footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid commercial registry certificate, tax card, board resolution authorizing account opening, shareholders' register, beneficial ownership declaration, registered office lease, business plan, forecast cash flows, supplier and customer contracts, and six months of banking or payment-provider statements where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear ultimate beneficial owner structure or use of offshore intermediate holding companies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full ownership chain to natural persons, passport/National ID copies, proof of residential address, source-of-wealth documentation, corporate constitutional docs for each intermediate entity, audited financial statements or opening balance sheets, and a signed CBE KYC/BO declaration.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume micro-transaction e-commerce collections from multiple foreign card/payment networks
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS attestation, Stripe/PayPal settlement statements with reconciliation, order-to-cash documentation, refund/chargeback policy, logistics/customs receipts, trademark/domain registration evidence, and transaction monitoring dashboards.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Supplier payments to high-risk jurisdictions or parties near the Egyptian sanctions perimeter
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening outputs (UN, EU, OFAC), end-user declarations, underlying invoices, Incoterms contracts, bill of lading/air waybill, customs import documentation, and written compliance certification from suppliers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected bank volume/velocity inconsistent with stated e-commerce retail business model
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Projected cash flow, payment-acquirer volume reports, tax return/withholding records, inventory purchase contracts, warehouse/logistics agreements, and evidence of foreign capital injection through regulated banking channels.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of local physical substance for a fully remote online retailer
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registered office agreement, local warehouse or fulfillment service provider contract, management structure table, board meeting minutes, and proof of local economic activity and decision-making substance.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity or shareholder-loan capital must be remitted by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign investor's bank account to the LLC's account at a licensed Egyptian bank using the CBE-designated purpose code for foreign direct investment or shareholder loan. The receiving bank must obtain a copy of the investment registration, board resolution, source-of-funds confirmation, and recorded CBE inward remittance form. The LLC must ensure the full wire narrative identifies the entity name, the registered investment certificate, and the underlying purpose; the bank then credits the proceeds and files with CBE's international transactions monitoring system. For capital amounts above CBE thresholds, pre-approval or registration with the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) is recommended.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements for inventory and logistics are cleared through SWIFT MT103/MT202 payments and, for larger or documentary-risk transactions, through irrevocable confirmed commercial letters of credit. The paying bank requires a compliant import payment application, underlying commercial contract, invoice, packing list, transport document, and customs declaration. The LLC must route all foreign payments through its licensed Egyptian bank; the bank may require document-linked FX approval and will debit the corresponding EGP or foreign-currency account. Cash-pooling and nostro/vostro correspondent clearing are managed through the bank's global correspondent network.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forwards with CBE-licensed banks, documented by real export/import exposure and limited to the underlying commercial transaction tenor
Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on EGP/USD arranged with licensed Egyptian banks or their international branches for repatriation risk management
Cross-currency swaps (USD/EGP and EUR/EGP) used to hedge long-term shareholder loans, subject to CBE exposure documentation
FX swaps combining spot and forward legs for short-term liquidity and working-capital hedging
Covered FX options and structured hedging products offered by licensed banks where the bank confirms the commercial underlying and obtains CBE-approval if required

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form 9) for juridical persons
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) – Corporate Income Tax Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April (within 4 months of the 31 December fiscal year-end for calendar-year taxpayers; equivalent anniversary rule for ETA-approved off-calendar fiscal years)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Delay fines of 10% of the tax due once the return is more than 60 days late, plus monthly delay penalties capped at 50% of the assessed tax; ex parte administrative assessment; criminal fines on responsible officers; enforced collection via bank liens and customs restrictions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements (balance sheet, income statement, cash-flow statement and auditor's report) deposited with the Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholder approval within 6 months of the fiscal year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies); registry deposit within 30 days after approval and in no event later than 30 July
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000 against the LLC, with manager(s) jointly and severally liable; two consecutive years of non-filing allow GAFI to administratively dissolve the company and strike off its commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Assembly of shareholders/quota-holders approving the financial statements, reappointing the auditor, and resolving dividend distribution; signed minutes retained in the corporate minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – Companies Registry (minutes and resolutions filed as attachments to the annual financial statements)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Convened within 6 months of the fiscal year-end (by 30 June for calendar-year companies); minutes archived at the registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Managers who fail to convene the assembly or present audited accounts are personally liable for resulting company losses and regulatory fines; the registry may petition the competent court for judicial dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration certificate renewal, annual good-standing confirmation, and amendments of registered particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Commercial Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Certificate renewal every 5 years from the registration anniversary; annual good-standing confirmation by each registration anniversary; amendments to managers, registered address and shareholders filed within 30 days of occurrence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fees up to EGP 2,000 per omitted amendment; temporary suspension of the commercial certificate; block on customs and import operations; revocation of the registration for continuing non-compliance.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) confirmation lodged on the electronic AML register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) – central UBO electronic register operated via the GAFI portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual zero-change confirmation by 31 March; UBO changes arising from share transfers declared within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EGP 500,000 and criminal imprisonment for deliberate concealment of beneficial ownership; default terminates banking and payment-service-provider onboarding.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual stamp tax declaration and settlement on the audited financial statements and corporate instruments
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority – Stamp Tax Department
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 30 April, aligned with the corporate income tax return (within 4 months of the fiscal year-end); stamping completed before the GAFI deposit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Double stamp-duty surcharge plus daily delay penalties; unstamped financial statements refused by GAFI and inadmissible before courts; criminal fines on managers under the Stamp Tax Law No. 111 of 1980.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory for every Egyptian LLC without size-based exemption; the Companies Law requires at least one independent certified public accountant registered on the ETA auditor registry, re-appointed annually by the general assembly, and the auditor's report must accompany the financial statements filed with the Companies Registry.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), issued by the Egyptian Ministry of Finance and substantially aligned with IFRS; books kept in Arabic; financial statements must present a true and fair view (IFRS consolidated reporting may additionally be required for group holding structures).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Egyptian LLCs must enrol in the EMLCU/GAFI UBO electronic register and maintain a physical UBO register at the registered office. Quota transfers take legal effect only upon registration in the Register of Members and must be reported to EMLCU within 30 days; where ownership is unchanged, an annual confirmation is lodged by 31 March. Managers and nominee disclosers remain continuously liable for accurate UBO data.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 – 1,500 per year for a serviced office or registered-address arrangement in Cairo, Alexandria, or the Suez Canal Economic Zone; a physical registered office in Egypt is mandatory
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 800 – 2,500 per year for a small-size e-commerce retail LLC; USD 3,500 – 6,000 per year where the audit is carried out by a Big-4 local affiliate or the group requires IFRS consolidation

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday for retail trade; small enterprises may benefit from reduced effective rates under ETA administrative guidance; however a pure internet retailing entity is not eligible for strategic investment incentives under Law No. 72 of 2017.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate Income Tax Return Form (Tax Declaration No. 1) filed electronically through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) online portal at www.eta.gov.eg
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return with quarterly advance self-assessment payments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return due within four months after the end of the fiscal year; quarterly advance payments due by the end of the first, second, and third months of each tax period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification: ETA tax card number, commercial registration number, and national ID/incorporation number of the entity
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the ETA-issued non-resident taxpayer identification number and the overseas jurisdiction ID; attach proof of PE status or treaty protection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period: start and end dates of the fiscal year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the same fiscal year as declared in the corporate accounting framework; confirm whether the entity has elected a different tax year under ETA approval.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit or loss before tax as per Egyptian accounting standards
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident filing a branch return, report Egypt-source profit segregated from overseas profit; if no PE, report nil and attach a Position Paper.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation adjustments: disallowed expenses, exempt income, depreciation, provisions, and transfer pricing adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible items include Egyptian corporate tax paid, dividends received from unrelated entities to the extent exempt, and provisions exceeding ETA limits; TP adjustments must be supported with contemporaneous documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income computed after applying adjustments and loss carryforward deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply treaty-dependent PE income allocation methodologies; ensure permanent establishment attribution of internet sales revenue is consistent with Article 7 of the applicable DTA.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax rate and final corporate income tax payable
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the 22.5% statutory rate for a juridical person; apply reduced withholding-based final taxes where the entity elects elective-held regime under ETA safe harbour rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Advance payments, foreign tax credits, and other refundable offsets
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Foreign Tax Credit Calculation Schedule under Egyptian unilateral relief rules if double taxation arises outside treaty scope.
If no PE and treaty claim applies, file refund application within five years of the end of the calendar year in which tax was paid.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty of not less than EGP 500 per month of delay and not more than EGP 1,000, plus a monthly delayed-payment surcharge of 1.5% on unpaid tax, capped at 100% of the underlying tax; false statements and willful omission attract an additional penalty equal to 100% of tax evaded.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final dividend withholding tax under Article 56 of the Egyptian Income Tax Law No. 91 of 2005.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply treaty relief, the foreign beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home jurisdiction, complete ETA Form 16 (Authorized Officer / Beneficial Owner Certificate), provide a legalized certificate of incorporation or equivalent, and submit the application to the ETA before distribution. If approved prior to payment, the reduced withholding rate is applied at source; otherwise the excess withholding may be claimed via the annual tax return or separate refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory rates: 20% on IP royalties and 20% on debt interest. Under Egyptian double tax treaties, royalty withholding rates typically range from 10% to 20% and interest rates from 10% to 15%, subject to active business or beneficial ownership clauses; treaty relief requires submission of TRC, Form 16, and underlying loan/licence documentation.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File must be prepared when annual related-party transactions exceed EGP 8 million; Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated annual turnover exceeding EGP 100 million or when a single related-party transaction exceeds EGP 20 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not maintain a separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) regime; however, the general anti-avoidance rule in Article 113 of Law 91/2005 and the Tax Fraud Law (Law 30 of 2020) authorize the ETA to disregard arrangements lacking commercial substance. For an internet retailer, material substance indicators include a physical Egyptian management office, inventory warehousing, purchase and sales contracts executed in Egypt, an operating Egyptian bank account, and autonomous pricing/risk control over the digital sales channel.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting marketplace sales by routing payments through personal Stripe or PayPal accounts; underreporting revenue from online camping equipment sales; destroying digital records of purchase orders and logistics invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Additional tax equal to 100% of the evaded tax, an administrative fine up to EGP 100,000, and monthly postponement surcharges; criminal conviction for intentional evasion can yield imprisonment up to five years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved or knew of the evasion are jointly and severally liable for corporate tax debts; courts may issue travel bans, freeze personal bank accounts, and impose prison sentences under Article 137 of Law 91/2005.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Forming an Egyptian LLC solely to obtain a tax card and channel foreign e-commerce transactions without genuine staff, sales activity, or risk management; declaring inventory in contracts while fulfillment is performed entirely outside Egypt without reflecting it in Egyptian books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA may nullify the tax registration, disallow treaty benefits, recharacterise income, and impose back-tax assessments plus 100% penalty on any unpaid tax; registration may also be revoked under anti-shell directives.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are liable in restitution for the full tax and penalties; where false declarations were submitted, imprisonment from one to five years is possible, and the responsible shareholder may be personally stripped of limited liability protection.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Funnelling customer payments through foreign PSP accounts without proper Egyptian business banking; failure to file beneficial ownership declarations; structuring transactions to avoid automatic ETA or AML reporting thresholds; involvement of politically exposed cross-border partners in revenue collection.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fines under Egypt AML Law No. 80 of 2002 as amended, ranging up to EGP 100,000 per violation, alongside suspension of the tax card and administrative delisting from export support programs; the ETA may also impose a 4% transaction-based anti-money laundering levy.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face imprisonment between one and ten years for laundering proceeds generated through such payment structures; assets and bank accounts can be seized; travel restricted until full restitution is made.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting profit margins below arm's length for an overseas procurement affiliate; failing to prepare Local File after related-party purchases exceed EGP 8 million; submitting a Tax Declaration with coordinated but false invoice documentation from a related party.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment increasing taxable income, plus 100% tax evasion penalty if the mispricing was willful; refusal to produce documentation triggers an administrative penalty of up to 1% of the value of undocumented transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign inaccurate Form 16 certificates or certified TP disclosures may be personally assessed for the resulting tax deficiency; if fraud is established, they are jointly liable for restitution and subject to imprisonment up to five years.
